@cloudbase/node-sdk > axios.reason: Same-source 0.x maintenance branch; 0.30.x is still affected by later advisory ranges. Existing SDK metadata and extension APIs passed compatibility tests.

@cloudbase/database > lodash.unset.reason: Same-source and same-major published modular package fix; ordinary path semantics and blocked prototype deletion paths passed regression tests.

reachabilityReview.trigger: Realtime partial update with updatedFields invokes set(doc, fieldPath, value).
reachabilityReview.applicationReview: index.js, service.cjs and repository.cjs do not call watch or accept updatedFields/field paths; repository uses doc.get, doc.set with rebuilt objects, scoped where/orderBy/limit/get and runTransaction.
reachabilityReview.conclusion: The vulnerable function is present in the installed dependency graph; the current application does not invoke the identified watch update path. This is source-level reachability evidence, not a claim that the upstream vulnerability is fixed or every possible runtime path was proven unreachable.

notes: Audit counts refer to affected packages: four high entries propagate from the same remaining lodash.set advisory, not four separate root advisories.
After overrides npm audit recommends a semver-major downgrade to wx-server-sdk 1.8.3; this was not applied.
Replacing @cloudbase/database 1.4.3 with latest 2.0.0 would cross an upstream major version and was not silently forced.

Axios 0.x maintenance releases include security-driven behavior changes; tests cover actual SDK metadata request and callable extension-shim shapes, not live cloud networking, proxies or every Axios feature.

The lodash.set/unset imports in the pinned database source are in realtime/virtual-websocket-client.ts; this service does not invoke realtime watch APIs. lodash.unset is patched; lodash.set has no same-package fixed release.
This service exposes no caller-controlled URLs, database paths, query expressions or nested arbitrary update objects. Inputs are strictly whitelisted.

Deploy with npm that supports overrides (>=8.3.0) and the committed lockfile; prefer npm ci and uploading the built dependency bundle. Remote dependency installation must preserve the same resolved versions.

Application input restrictions limit reachable attack paths but do not mean dependency findings are cleared. Real-cloud identity, database transactions, permissions, indexes and two-account integration remain unverified without an actual AppID/environment.
